source.title: Sparse Autoencoders enable Robust and Interpretable Fine-tuning of CLIP models
source.authors: Fabian Morelli; Arnas Uselis; Ankit Sonthalia; S. Oh

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures SAE feature reconstruction and overlap in CLIP visual representations, extending evidence about dictionary-recoverable features to a vision-language model setting; it does not reproduce the toy-model experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper reports SAE reconstruction error (FVU), feature overlap, and feature-task alignment for CLIP representations; these bear on SAE-recoverable features and their stability across fine-tuning. Its discussion of superposition and polysemanticity is background, not a new test of toy-model superposition. Classification performance tables and values used only for hyperparameter selection are not recorded as claim rows.
record.test_reason: The paper is a CLIP fine-tuning method study. It uses a Top-K SAE trained on zero-shot CLIP vision embeddings as a regulariser and analysis tool, and reports mainly its own method's performance. The SAE metrics (FVU, feature overlap) measure how far fine-tuned models drift from the zero-shot model's dictionary. That is representational drift between different models, not whether one model's features are SAE-recoverable or are its canonical units. The setting is a CLIP vision encoder, not an LLM, so V4's named system kind does not match. Superposition and polysemanticity appear only as cited background.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also conclude that standard fine-tuning collapses the zero-shot SAE dictionary (FVU>1, ~80% of features lost), which motivates the method. They state that SAE-FT's gains over L2 regularisation are marginal and that its value lies in interpretability and control over which features change.
record.recipe_differences: This is a CLIP fine-tuning study using a Top-K SAE as a representation regularizer, not a reproduction of the original toy-network superposition experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that SAE architecture choices, including the number of active features and dictionary multiplier, change downstream distribution-shift performance; it does not report an SAE reconstruction-metric sweep over those choices.

fits_no_version.finding: An SAE trained on zero-shot CLIP ViT-B/16 vision embeddings reconstructs standard fine-tuned embeddings worse than a mean baseline (FVU 1.28). It keeps only about 19% (FT) or 43% (WiSE-FT) of active features. L2-regularised fine-tuning keeps FVU at 0.23 but overlap at 0.67.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning CLIP vision encoders shifts representations so that a dictionary learned on the pre-trained model no longer fits, unless drift is explicitly regularised.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE-FT and L2 fine-tuning increase the activation-weighted alignment of active SAE directions with the correct class embedding.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Regularised fine-tuning re-weights existing SAE features toward class-aligned directions.

record.problems: The evidence is limited to CLIP visual representations and does not test LLM or text-encoder representations. The authors note SAE-FT's sensitivity to SAE architecture. Several feature metrics are reported without uncertainty estimates; standard deviations are reported for some other experiments.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying results were omitted. Classification accuracy comparisons and hyperparameter-selection values were excluded because they do not directly measure SAE feature recovery, overlap, or the claim's other named properties.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity transition or geometry.
No test of capacity competition or dedicated dimensions.
No test of other causes of polysemanticity.
No LLM representations. Does not measure whether features are spread across neurons. SAE recovery in CLIP vision is only used as a tool.
No test of completeness, canonicality, or stability across SAE seeds or sizes for a fixed model. The architecture ablation reports downstream accuracy only.
No comparison of 1-D and multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: Method paper with the SAE as a tool. Table 7 values duplicate Table 2 for zero-shot and L2. SAE-FT rows are own-method outcomes of a feature-preserving penalty. CLIP vision is outside V4's named LLM setting. No verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, more sparse features than dimensions, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry are not tested.
The paper does not test whether neuron polysemanticity results from capacity competition or whether important features obtain dedicated dimensions.
The paper does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
The study tests SAE reconstruction of CLIP visual representations, not LLM representations, text-encoder features, or whether features are spread across many neurons.

It measures the fixed dictionary's reconstruction and feature overlap across fine-tuned representations, but does not test whether SAE features are complete, canonical, or stable across independently trained dictionaries.
The study treats SAE decoder features as directions but does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional features.

relation.reason: Relies on sparse semantic directions to constrain CLIP vision representations without testing superposition or whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical representational units.

tranche.reason: Uses a fixed SAE as a fine-tuning regularizer and analysis tool. Reconstruction, feature overlap and task alignment characterize representation drift and method performance; they do not test the listed superposition versions.

source_check.notes: Section 4 describes FVU > 1 using a zero-vector baseline, but Appendix B defines its baseline as the empirical mean; the row note accurately reports the former wording. Tables 2 and 7 repeat reference and L2 values; SAE-FT results are method outcomes, not independent evidence for claim versions.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Zero-shot and regularized ViT-B/16 visual representations
reader_labels.reason: The zero-shot SAE has low FVU on zero-shot, L2-regularized, and SAE-FT representations, consistent with SAE-recoverable features in this setting (r1, r4, r9, r10, r11).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The fixed zero-shot SAE reconstructs standard fine-tuned representations poorly and WiSE-FT representations less well than the zero-shot baseline (r2, r3).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The fixed SAE's FVU rises to 1.28 and feature overlap falls to 0.19, challenging stability of the original feature dictionary under standard fine-tuning (r2, r6).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Reconstruction is relatively good for regularized models, but feature overlap is below the zero-shot reference, including 0.43 for WiSE-FT, 0.67 for L2 regularization, and 0.78 for SAE-FT (r3, r4, r7, r8, r10, r11, r13, r14).
